title: Spotlight tiles + pivot steps: Quickstart landing visual refresh
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Background: The current Quickstart landing hero and step visuals are information-dense and don't clearly communicate the value props for first-time developer signups. Goal: Design a concise, scannable hero with 'spotlight tiles' that surface three starter flows (SDKs, Hosted API, Private deployment), and a progressive 'pivot steps' visual that adapts from mobile to desktop. Scope: hero composition, three spotlight tiles (icons + 1-line benefits), a condensed step-by-step diagram for the quickstart flow, responsive screenshots for docs, and handoff spec for engineering and content. Deliverables: hi-fi hero mockups (desktop/tablet/mobile), annotated component spec, export-ready SVG icons, responsive screenshots showing real console state, and a short animation prototype for micro-interactions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Hero communicates top 3 quickstart paths in under 3 seconds. 2) Spotlight tiles have accessible contrast and readable labels at 320px width. 3) Step diagram compresses into stacked cards on mobile while preserving visual relationships. 4) Provided assets include SVGs, 2x/3x PNGs for screenshots, and a documented CSS spacing/token map. 5) Design review sign-off from PM and Eng with a follow-up implementation ticket.
tasks: Research competitor quickstart hero patterns and summarize findings (Aisha)
Sketch 4 layout variants and circulate for team preference (Marco)
Create color/token proposals for spotlight accents and surface contrast tests
Design desktop hero with spotlight tiles and CTA variants (primary/secondary)
Design mobile-responsive versions and stacking rules
Build step-diagram as accessible HTML/CSS demo for handoff
Export SVG icon set and guidance for icon swapping per flow
Prepare screenshot script and capture console sample flows for assets
Write annotation document: spacing, responsive breakpoints, interactions
Schedule design review and incorporate feedback
design_decisions: We will surface three starter paths as 'spotlight tiles' rather than a long feature list to reduce cognitive load. Each tile will have a subtle gradient accent (single accent color per tile) to help scanning, but the main text will use neutral typography for accessibility. The step diagram will use a pivot layout: horizontal progression on wide screens and stacked cards with connective dots on narrow screens. Motion is limited to micro-transitions for tile hover and a simplified step reveal to avoid performance cost on page load.
accessibility_notes: All buttons and tiles must pass AA contrast; focus states will be visible for keyboard nav; iconography will have aria-hidden=true with text alternatives provided. Provide tokenized color and spacing values for engineering. Test with screen reader to ensure step ordering remains logical when stacked.
blockers: Need engineering confirm on available hero height constraints across target platforms
Access to a staging console user for screenshot captures (awaiting ENG-12098)
review_comments: PM: Prefer more emphasis on 'Start in minutes' messaging — reduce copy length on tiles (from Content)
Eng: Concern about animation jank on older devices; recommend providing static fallback and reduced-motion variant
Design lead: iterate on icon metaphors for 'Private' tile to avoid security misinterpretation
handoff_notes: Deliver Figma frames grouped by breakpoint, a single-page HTML/CSS demo for the step diagram, and a zipped assets folder (SVGs + optimized PNGs). Include a short video (10-15s) demonstrating tile hover and step reveal for the launch page. Provide a checklist for QA: token verification, responsive breakpoints, focus order, and reduced-motion test.
notes: Aim to A/B test two headline copies in the first week after deployment: 'Get started with Redwood in minutes' vs 'Production-ready inference, first request fast'. Track sign-up conversion lift and time-to-first-request metrics.
implementation_plan: 1) Finalize designs and export assets (Design). 2) Eng builds static hero and responsive CSS with accessible markup. 3) Integrate screenshots and microcopy (Content). 4) QA and accessibility testing. 5) Launch behind feature flag, monitor conversions and performance. Create follow-up tickets for tweaks post-launch.
